items.claim: Every Hebrew fact the row asserts is true on the bytes - the dateline at MT 29:1 (tenth year, tenth month, twelfth day) with the perfect-form word-event in the same verse, the turn to Pharaoh at MT 29:2, the messenger formula at MT 29:3, the two variant sites at MT 29:4 and MT 29:7, the paseq count at MT 29:3 with no within-verse position asserted, and the strict-family refrain inside MT 29:9 - but the close-side warrant for the seam after MT 29:9 is formula-only: the single parashah mark inside the span is a setumah after MT 29:7, which makes MT 29:8 a paragraph onset in the tradition, and the row weighs MT 29:6 as its alternative while the mark-supported joint at MT 29:7/29:8 is disclosed and left unweighed. Confidence high overstates that close side.
items.both_sides: Onset side, strong: MT 29:1 carries a dateline of the book's fourteen together with the perfect-form word-event of its seven-verse set, MT 29:2 turns the address to Pharaoh, MT 29:3 opens the verdict on the messenger formula, and the mark inventory records a setumah after MT 28:26, immediately behind the onset. Close side, weaker: the refrain וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה inside MT 29:9 belongs to the 28-verse strict close family and MT 29:10 opens לָכֵ֛ן הִנְנִ֥י אֵלֶ֖יךָ, so a cycle does end at MT 29:9; against that, the tradition's paragraph here runs MT 29:8 to MT 29:12 (its next mark is a petuchah after MT 29:12), so the proposed close falls inside one Masoretic paragraph, and the causal clause יַ֧עַן אָמַ֛ר יְאֹ֥ר לִ֖י וַאֲנִ֥י עָשִֽׂיתִי that ends MT 29:9 is answered by MT 29:10, so the seam as placed separates an indictment from the verdict it governs. The chapter runs that pair twice: יַ֧עַן הֱיוֹתָ֛ם מִשְׁעֶ֥נֶת קָנֶ֖ה at MT 29:6 is answered by לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הִנְנִ֛י at MT 29:8, and it is exactly at that first joint - after the indictment, before the verdict - that the tradition put its mark. Both readings are live on the bytes, so the label moves and the seam does not.

suggested_fix.fact: a setumah stands after MT 29:7, making MT 29:8 a paragraph onset in the tradition, so the alternative seam to weigh from both sides is MT 29:7/29:8 beside MT 29:6

items.claim: The close at MT 29:16 is read correctly as a wide-family recognition close rather than the strict refrain: the verse ends וְיָ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֥י אֲנִ֖י אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה, the divine-name pair standing where the strict form carries the bare name, which is why the verse is outside the 28-verse strict set; a petuchah follows MT 29:16; and the forty-year statements at MT 29:11, MT 29:12 and MT 29:13 are duration language, not datelines, exactly as the book's own date inventory records them.
items.both_sides: Onset side: MT 29:10 is the second of the chapter's two indictment-verdict turns and sits inside the Masoretic paragraph that opens at MT 29:8, so that edge is formula-supported and mark-unsupported, which the medium label already carries. Close side: the refrain at MT 29:16 is corroborated by a petuchah after that verse and the next verse carries the book's latest dateline, so the close edge is doubly warranted. The strongest competitor inside the span is the petuchah after MT 29:12 with a messenger formula at MT 29:13; against a cut there, that formula stands under a subordinating particle - כִּ֛י כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה - which binds it to the verdict it follows instead of opening a fresh speech, and the row's ground for calling the recurrence paragraph marking is therefore supported by the bytes and not only by the absence of a refrain.

suggested_fix.fact: the messenger formula at MT 29:13 stands under a subordinating particle, unlike the asyndetic formula onsets in this block; that is the positive byte ground for treating the petuchah after MT 29:12 as paragraph marking rather than a unit seam

items.claim: The onset is cited in the right member of the word-event family: MT 29:17 reads וַיְהִ֗י בְּעֶשְׂרִ֤ים וָשֶׁ֨בַע֙ שָׁנָ֔ה and then הָיָ֥ה דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר, so the row is right to call it the perfect form that a dated oracle uses after its date rather than the strict form, and right that this is the latest of the book's fourteen datelines. Both edges are mark-corroborated - a petuchah after MT 29:16 behind the onset and a petuchah after MT 29:21 at the close - the two setumahs inside the span, after MT 29:18 and after MT 29:20, are both disclosed, and the span holds no variant site and no paseq, as the row states.
items.both_sides: Onset side: a petuchah stands after MT 29:16, MT 29:17 carries the dateline plus the perfect-form word-event, and MT 29:18 carries the son-of-man address. Close side: the refrain וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה ends MT 29:21 and a petuchah follows it, while the next verse opens an undated oracle on the strict-form word-event וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר. The competitor inside the span is the utterance formula at MT 29:20 with a setumah after that verse; against closing there, MT 29:21 opens on a bare temporal phrase and carries no onset device of its own, so the refrain one verse later is the unit-final close and the mark after MT 29:20 is internal paragraphing.

items.claim: The distinctive Hebrew claim is true and checkable: MT 30:6 carries the short messenger form כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה, without the divine-name pair, and a skeleton sweep of the whole witness finds that form in exactly three verses, so the row's count is right. Its three internal marks are all disclosed (petuchah after MT 30:5, setumah after MT 30:9, setumah after MT 30:12), the emphatic close אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי ends MT 30:12 and a setumah follows that verse, and the undated strict-form onset at MT 30:1 is correctly distinguished from the dated openings of the preceding chapter.
items.both_sides: Onset side: a petuchah stands after MT 29:21, MT 30:1 carries the strict-form word-event with no date, and MT 30:2 carries the son-of-man command with the messenger formula. Close side: the emphatic close inside MT 30:12 is followed by a setumah, and MT 30:13 opens asyndetically on כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה. The strongest counter-configuration inside the span is MT 30:9/30:10, where a recognition refrain stands at MT 30:8, a setumah follows MT 30:9 and a messenger formula opens MT 30:10 - nearly the pattern the row uses at its own close; it is weaker because the refrain does not stand in the verse the mark follows, which is the distinction the row draws, and the medium label carries the residue of a span that crosses three Masoretic paragraphs.

items.claim: Both edges of this unit are corroborated by the parashah layer - a setumah follows MT 30:12 and a petuchah follows MT 30:19 - the refrain וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה ends MT 30:19 and belongs to the strict close family, the onset at MT 30:13 is the asyndetic כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה, the variant site at MT 30:16 is named without the apparatus string being rendered, and the row's statement that the city roster at MT 30:14-30:18 carries no internal formula seam is true: no messenger, utterance, recognition or son-of-man form falls in those five verses.
items.both_sides: Onset side: the emphatic close ends MT 30:12, a setumah follows that verse, and MT 30:13 opens on the messenger formula with no particle before it and no change of addressee. Close side: the refrain ends MT 30:19, a petuchah follows it, and the next verse carries a dateline of the book's fourteen, so the close edge is warranted from both the formula layer and the mark layer. Against a cut at the onset: the addressee does not change and no therefore-clause precedes, which is what the row concedes and what holds the label at medium.
